summary: the observed order of convergence of a quantity from three runs at a constant refinement ratio

inputs.name: coarse
inputs.meaning: the quantity from the coarsest of the three runs, in its unit

inputs.name: medium
inputs.meaning: the same quantity from the middle run, in the same unit

inputs.name: fine
inputs.meaning: the same quantity from the finest run, in the same unit

inputs.name: refinement_ratio
inputs.meaning: the constant ratio of each run's spacing to the next finer one's, above 1

outputs.name: observed
outputs.meaning: true when an order was read from the three results; false, with why, when they do not converge monotonically or the inputs do not allow it

outputs.name: why
outputs.meaning: why no order was read, or null

validity: three runs of one scheme on the same problem, each finer than the last by the same ratio, in the asymptotic range and converging monotonically; where the differences change sign there is no order to read. It keeps no safety factor (the person, 2026-11-18), and judges nothing

source.citation: NASA Glenn Research Center, NPARC Alliance CFD Verification and Validation, Examining Spatial (Grid) Convergence (read 2026-11-18, https://www.grc.nasa.gov/www/wind/valid/tutorial/spatconv.html; meta_agent/inbox/materials/20261118-nasa-grc-spatial-convergence, v3_RETRIEVED.json)
source.locus: section Order of Grid Convergence: a more direct evaluation of p from three solutions at a constant grid refinement ratio r, p = ln((f3 - f2)/(f2 - f1)) / ln(r), f1 the finest, read off its image eq_porder1.gif

note: Made for a scientific task's refinement with a third run (the intake card's third_inputs, 6c7a488; failures.jsonl cfd-25), so that the run's own error needs no order from a source; a common skill of meta_agent/tasks/025.
